subject: System Design
title: Stripe's Payment Flow
description: A 60-second lesson on Stripe's Payment Flow.

hook.text: You enter your card on a website and click pay. Seven different systems coordinate to move money — in under 3 seconds.

buildup.text: The merchant's server sends card details to Stripe. Stripe contacts the card network which contacts your bank.

discovery.text: Authorization, capture, and settlement are separate steps. The money isn't moved instantly — it settles days later.

twist.text: A payment can be authorized (funds held) but never captured. The hold expires after days. No money actually moved.

climax.text: Payments are multi-party distributed transactions with eventual settlement — not instant money transfers.

punchline.text: Authorize now, capture later, settle in days — payments aren't instant.

quiz.question: What is the difference between authorization and settlement?
options: Authorization holds funds; settlement actually moves the money days later
